It will also aim to give continuity to their research career, in a second phase of the grant, which will enable them to improve their training and establish their own line of research that will allow them, in the future, to consolidate their career. The training programme is divided into two phases: - Phase 1 (3 years) : Research stay abroad of 20 to 24 months. Two stays of at least 12 months each can be carried out in different centres. - Phase 2 (3 years) : at UVigo. An interim assessment takes place after phase 1. If this is not passed, access to phase 2 is not possible. The monthly gross salary is approximately 2030€ in phase 1 and 2300€ in phase 2 . The Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) must have been obtained after 1 January 2014 . The doctorate must have been obtained after 1 January 2020 . There is one modality, Fullbright , for conducting Phase 1 stays in the United States. The stay must be continuous and last between 20 and 24 months. The following criteria are considered when evaluating applications for Phase 1: - Scientific publications (maximum 40 points). Books with ISBNs and articles receive more points than book chapters. Gross Monthly salary : 1.900,00 € (including the apportionments of extra payments) Expected starting date : 6 March Workday: Full Time (37.5 hours per week) Employment status: Support technician C Place of Work: Pontevedra The Post-Growth Innovation Lab at the University of Vigo invites applications for a research support technitian in the project A Right to a Repair Society: Controversies, Opportunities, and Challenges (ATTRACT) . This project investigates how the Right to Repair (R2R) movement can contribute to a post-growth society while addressing the environmental and social challenges posed by consumer electronics. The full job offer can be found at the following link: https://secretaria.uvigo.gal/uv/web/convocatoria/public/show/1514 (external link) PROJECT OVERVIEW The Right to Repair (R2R) movement advocates for greater rights and collective freedoms to repair our electronic devices, countering manufacturer practices like planned obsolescence. By promoting repairability, R2R aims to reduce electronic waste, limit resource extraction, and foster sustainable consumption practices. This project will map the multiple perspectives surrounding the R2R debate and analyse how these perspectives influence EU legislation on sustainability and circular economy. While mapping out these different perspectives is essential, the project places a strong focus on how they are being integrated in actual R2R legislation, particularly within the European Union. Finally, the project will analyse these dynamics in terms of their alignment with the transition to a post-growth economy. ATTRACT Project (Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities) Supervisors : Dr. Javier Lloveras (external link) and Dr. Mario Pansera (external link) Project Title : A Right to a Repair Society: Controversies, Opportunities, and Challenges (ATTRACT) Funding Duration : 4 years Gross salary : approx €23000 per year Scholarship type: Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities Expected starting date : December 2024-January 2025 NEW PRE-APPLICATION DEADLINE : 15 October The Post-Growth Innovation Lab at the University of Vigo invites applications for a fully funded PhD position in the project A Right to a Repair Society: Controversies, Opportunities, and Challenges (ATTRACT) . This project investigates how the Right to Repair (R2R) movement can contribute to a post-growth society while addressing the environmental and social challenges posed by consumer electronics. PROJECT OVERVIEW The Right to Repair (R2R) movement advocates for greater rights and collective freedoms to repair our electronic devices, countering manufacturer practices like planned obsolescence. By promoting repairability, R2R aims to reduce electronic waste, limit resource extraction, and foster sustainable consumption practices. This project will map the multiple perspectives surrounding the R2R debate and analyse how these perspectives influence EU legislation on sustainability and circular economy. While mapping out these different perspectives is essential, the project places a strong focus on how they are being integrated in actual R2R legislation , particularly within the European Union . Finally, the project will analyse these dynamics in terms of their alignment with the transition to a post-growth economy. PhD CANDIDATE PROFILE We welcome applicants from any academic background—be it social sciences, humanities, or natural sciences—as long as they possess the necessary skills and motivations required for the project. Below is a detailed list of the essential skills we are looking for. While it’s not necessary to meet every single criterion, these are the qualities we will prioritize when shortlisting candidates. The ideal candidate will have the following essential skills : A good understanding of the EU legislative process in relevant areas. Experience working with qualitative research methods (e.g., interviews, discourse analysis) and a disposition to develop their qualitative research skills further. Critical thinking and ability to review and synthesize academic literature across various disciplines and fields. Experience conducting systematic literature reviews – or at least, a reasonable understanding of this process. A good understanding of postgrowth/degrowth theories. Availability to travel for fieldwork. Proven ability to carry out academic work in English (writing, reading, and speaking). Ability to communicate in Spanish language is not mandatory but advisable. Autonomy, resilience, and an ability to conduct academic work independently. Teamwork skills and the ability to collaborate effectively. ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS · Candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree, or equivalent, and a Master's degree, or equivalent, provided they have completed at least 300 ECTS credits in the two types of programmes as a whole. · We invited candidates from any discipline to apply. RESPONSIBILITIES To work on a full time PhD whose content will be directly aligned with the general project aim and objectives Conduct a rigorous, systematic review of relevant literature Conduct qualitative research, including aspects of research design, fieldwork, and data analysis. Engage with and collect data from multiple stakeholders in the Right to Repair debate in the EU. From consumer groups to policy makers, to activists and NGOs, etc. Contribute to publications, policy briefs, and public outreach as part of the project. BENEFITS Full funding for 4 years . The opportunity to contribute to innovative research at the intersection of sustainability, postgrowth, and EU policy. Access to international academic and policy networks. Support for career development, including opportunities for publication and participation in international conferences. HOW TO APPLY The application process is divided in two stages (pre-application and formal application). Only shortlisted candidates will be asked to formally apply to the University of Vigo, with detailed instructions provided at that stage. Following the formal application process, interviews will be conducted. Deadline for pre-applications is 15 October . The following documents are required for this pre-application (sent to this e-mail address: postgrowth-lab@uvigo.es (external link) ): Curriculum Vitae (CV) highlighting areas that are relevant to the project A cover letter outlining their research interests and motivation for applying, including how their background fits the project At least one reference letter (preferably two) from relevant referees. A brief research proposal (max. 1,000 words) on how they would approach the PhD topic. The following documents will be later required for the shortlisted applicants invited to make formal application : Abbreviated CV, following the standardized format ( https://cvn.fecyt.es/ (external link) ), with specific emphasis on scientific and technical contributions, as well as international experience and mobility. Academic transcripts. Grading scale and equivalencies (external link) (only for those studies completed outside the Spanish system), formally signed by the issuing institution (external link) . This applies only to foreign degrees. Africa , PhD , Scholarships , South America | 0 | Spread the love The University of Bonn and Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences are inviting applications for 10 doctoral research positions under the DFG Research Training Group (RTG) “Urban Future – Managing Transformations for Better Health in Blue Cities.” The interdisciplinary doctoral programme focuses on the relationship between urbanisation, water, public health, ecological sustainability and social justice , with particular attention to cities located along rivers and coastlines. Starting in April 2027 , successful candidates will join a structured four-year doctoral programme that combines individual PhD research with interdisciplinary training, seminars, systems-thinking approaches, transdisciplinary research methods and professional development. The programme is particularly relevant to graduates interested in urban health, public health, climate change, water-health systems, governance, environmental sustainability, infectious diseases, urban planning, ecological systems, development studies and social sciences . Successful doctoral researchers will receive a four-year doctoral support contract with remuneration based on TV-L pay grade 13 (65%) , according to the German public-sector salary scale. Employment will be at either the University of Bonn or Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences. The application deadline is 19 October 2026 . About the Urban Future Research Training Group The DFG Research Training Group “Urban Future” examines how cities can manage urban transformations in ways that improve public health, ecological sustainability and social equity . The programme uses the concept of the “Blue City” to describe urban areas situated along rivers or coastlines where water is considered more than simply a resource or a potential hazard. Instead, water becomes an integral part of: Urban planning Infrastructure development Environmental management Public health Social systems Urban identity Climate adaptation Ecological sustainability The research programme recognises that cities are complex systems in which environmental, social, economic, political and health-related factors interact. Researchers will therefore investigate the connections between urban transformation, water-related challenges and health outcomes , particularly in rapidly changing urban environments. A major emphasis is placed on cities in the Global South , which serve as important living laboratories for understanding urban transformation and developing solutions that can contribute to healthier and more sustainable cities. However, applicants are not restricted to research sites in the Global South. Candidates are free to propose research sites in any Blue City worldwide , provided that the proposed research aligns with the objectives of the programme. Universities and International Research Network The Research Training Group is jointly operated by: University of Bonn Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences It works in cooperation with the German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS) and a network of international partner universities. The international partnership includes institutions in: Ghana Togo Cameroon Brazil Japan The listed partner institutions include: KNUST – Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana University of Ghana, Ghana University of Cape Coast, Ghana University of Lomé, Togo University of Buea, Cameroon University of São Paulo, Brazil The University of Tokyo, Japan This international structure gives doctoral researchers an opportunity to work within a research environment that connects European and Global South perspectives on urban health, sustainability and transformation. Four Research Themes of the Urban Future PhD Programme The doctoral programme is organised around four major interdisciplinary research themes. Research Theme A: Urban Health Resilience The Urban Health Resilience theme examines how urban communities respond to and recover from health pressures associated with water and environmental change. Research may focus on issues such as: Flooding Drought Urban heat islands Air pollution Unequal access to clean water Food systems Environmental exposures Mental health Social inequalities Climate adaptation Green and blue infrastructure The research theme combines perspectives from areas such as epidemiology, sociology, environmental science, urban planning and public health . Researchers will examine how communities can develop greater resilience while ensuring that vulnerable populations are not left behind. Successful candidates will receive a structured doctoral research experience rather than simply conducting an independent PhD project. The programme provides several forms of academic and professional support. 1. Four-Year Doctoral Support Contract The Research Training Group will begin on 1 April 2027 . Successful applicants will receive a four-year doctoral support contract , with remuneration dependent on TV-L pay grade 13 at 65% , in accordance with the German public salary scale. Employment will be at either: University of Bonn; or Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences. 2. Funded Research Expenses The programme states that fieldwork, travel and related research expenses are fully funded . This is particularly important for doctoral projects involving international fieldwork or research in different urban environments. 3. Structured Doctoral Training Doctoral researchers will participate in an interdisciplinary training programme covering areas such as: Systems thinking Transdisciplinary research Academic communication Interdisciplinary research Research methods Soft skills Professional development 4. Interdisciplinary Research Environment The programme brings together researchers from different academic disciplines. This allows doctoral candidates to examine urban health challenges from multiple perspectives rather than approaching them from a single discipline. 5. International Research Network Researchers will have access to a strong national and international network involving universities and research institutions in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America. 6. Career Development Support The programme also provides dedicated career development support , structured supervision and clear progression criteria. Responsibilities of Selected Doctoral Researchers Successful candidates will be expected to actively participate in the Research Training Group and contribute to its interdisciplinary research environment. Their responsibilities will include: Participating actively in the RTG training programme. Taking part in interdisciplinary seminars. Conducting independent doctoral research aligned with one of the four research themes. Developing appropriate research methodologies. Collecting and analysing research data. Publishing research findings. Contributing to the development of Blue City concepts. Participating in transdisciplinary knowledge exchange. The programme is seeking applicants who have already completed a Master’s degree or equivalent qualification in a relevant discipline. These include: Agricultural and Food Systems Climate and Earth Sciences Development Studies Ecology and Life Sciences Economics and Management Mathematics Physics Computer Science Environmental Sciences Health Sciences Geography Infectious Diseases Hygiene and Infection Control Medical Microbiology Public Health Urban and Regional Studies Social Sciences Applicants should also demonstrate: A strong interdisciplinary mindset A clear interest in urban transformation Interest in the water-health nexus and/or urban health Excellent written English Excellent spoken English English Language Requirement Applicants are required to provide evidence of English language proficiency at B2 level , according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), or an equivalent qualification such as TOEFL. Is the Opportunity Open to International Applicants? Yes. The programme has an explicitly international research orientation and involves partner institutions across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe . The call identifies partner institutions in Ghana, Togo, Cameroon, Brazil and Japan , while applicants are permitted to propose research sites in any Blue City worldwide . Therefore, the programme is not presented as being restricted to German or European applicants. Applicants should, however, ensure that they satisfy the academic, language and application requirements specified in the official call. Application Documents Required The application process consists of two stages . Applications will first be assessed by the RTG Selection Committee. Candidates considered among the most qualified will then be invited to participate in a virtual interview . Applicants are required to submit the following: 1. Curriculum Vitae A tabular-format CV should be provided, presenting the applicant’s academic background, professional experience, research experience, skills and other relevant information. 2. Degree Certificates and Transcripts Applicants must provide: Higher education degree certificate(s) Full transcript(s) of records An explanation of the grading system used for previous studies 3. Motivation Letter A motivation letter of no more than 500 words is required. The letter should explain the applicant’s motivation for joining the programme and demonstrate their interest in the relevant research area. 4. Research Exposé Applicants must submit a research exposé of no more than 1,500 words . This is an important part of the application because candidates are expected to propose doctoral research aligned with one of the programme’s four research themes. 5. Interdisciplinary Research Statement Applicants must provide an interdisciplinary research statement of no more than 500 words . This should demonstrate their ability to think across disciplinary boundaries and connect their proposed research with the wider objectives of the Research Training Group. 6. Letter of Recommendation Applicants must submit one letter of recommendation . 7. English Language Certificate Applicants must provide evidence of B2-level English proficiency , such as CEFR, TOEFL or an equivalent qualification. Application Deadline The deadline to submit a complete application is: 19 October 2026 Applicants should ensure that all required documents are prepared and submitted through the online application portal before the deadline. Candidates should also indicate the specific research theme they are applying for. Important Information About Gender Equality The call states that, in accordance with the Landesgleichstellungsgesetz (LGG) NRW , women will be given preference in cases where candidates have equal suitability, qualifications and professional performance, unless reasons relating to another candidate prevail. The programme also states that it is committed to diversity and equal opportunity and is certified as a family-friendly university . Why the Blue City Concept Matters The Blue City concept is central to the programme. Rather than treating water solely as something that cities need to control, remove or supply, the programme examines water as an important component of the urban environment. This approach can involve examining: Rivers Coastlines Flood management Water infrastructure Public health Urban ecosystems Climate resilience Green-blue infrastructure Water quality Urban planning Social equity Disease ecology Governance The programme therefore recognises that water-related challenges cannot always be addressed through engineering solutions alone. They may also require changes in governance, public policy, community participation, health systems, environmental management and urban planning.
